adminConsole.adminConsoleIsNotAvailable: Admin Console is not available for this account.

audit.noAuditEventsMatchThe: No audit events match the current filters.
audit.nothingHasChangedInThis: Nothing has changed in this workspace yet.
audit.theChangeHistoryIsNot: The change history is not available:

backupKey.aKeyIsEscrowedFor: A key is escrowed for this workspace, but its public half was not recorded, so it cannot be reused here. Paste it below.
backupKey.existingKey: The key this workspace already has
backupKey.existingKeyBody: Escrowed. Use it again so one key opens every backup this workspace makes.
backupKey.existingKeyBodyBy: Escrowed by {{who}}. Use it again so one key opens every backup this workspace makes.
backupKey.orADifferentKey: Or use a different public key
backupKey.ownKeyBody: Paste the public half of a key you hold. Nothing here ever sees the private one.
backupKey.pasteHint: The age1 line from age-keygen. Leave empty to keep using the escrowed key.
backupKey.platformKeyBody: Your provider can open the backup, so they can help you restore it. The right choice unless you have a reason otherwise.

backup.aBucketYouNameOn: A bucket you name, on a provider you name. For handing a copy to someone, or keeping one somewhere this platform cannot reach.
backup.aCopyKeptCloseFor: A copy kept close, for just before a risky change. It shares a home with the data it protects, so it is not what you want for disaster recovery.
backup.anExportCapturesThisTenant: An export captures this tenant — app databases, files and member accounts — into one encrypted bundle. Apps are paused one at a time while each is captured, so every app's data is internally consistent; the rest keep running.
backup.anExportIsAlreadyRunning: An export is already running. Only one runs at a time, so no app is paused by two at once.
backup.bundleStays: The bundle stays in the platform’s object storage at the location above. bundle-info.json inside it is readable and names the exact command that decrypts the rest.
backup.chDk2SomeProviders: ch-dk-2 — some providers need one, MinIO does not
backup.enterBothKeys: Enter both an access key and a secret key, or use the stored credentials.
backup.enterEndpoint: Enter the S3 endpoint to write this backup to.
backup.enterPublicKey: Enter the public key to encrypt this backup to.
backup.leaveEmptyToKeepThis: leave empty to keep this workspace's bucket name
backup.name: Name
backup.onlyYouCanOpenThis: Only you can open this bundle.
backup.passphraseBody: Encrypted so only you can open it — not the platform, not support. If the passphrase is lost, the bundle cannot be recovered by anyone.
backup.passphraseTooShort: Use a passphrase of at least 12 characters.
backup.pausedRightNow: Paused right now: {{apps}}. These apps stay offline until this export finishes.
backup.theCredentialsAlreadyHeldFor: The credentials already held for this workspace — the ones the nightly backup uses. Nothing to type, and nothing new to keep safe.
backup.theDestinationThisWorkspaceIs: The destination this workspace is configured for — the same place the nightly backup writes.
backup.usedForThisBackupOnly: Used for this backup only. They are kept while it runs and removed when it finishes — they are not stored for next time.

catalogue.installBody: Build <mono>{{digest}}</mono> of <mono>{{coordinate}}</mono>. Installing is a commit to the deployments repository with you as its author; the cluster has the app once that is synced.
catalogue.installEveryoneBody: Every member of this tenant has access by default; people invited later get it pre-selected.
catalogue.installPlainBody: Access is given per person, under Members.
catalogue.noDigest: not installable from here: the source states no digest for this entry
catalogue.nothingThisClusterListsFor: Nothing this cluster lists for itself.
catalogue.outcomeAlreadyInstalled: Nothing to commit — this tenant already has that build of <mono>{{app}}</mono>.
catalogue.outcomeEveryone: Every member of this tenant gets access once the app is ready.
catalogue.outcomeInstalled: Installing <mono>{{app}}</mono> was committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono> and arrives on the next sync. This list is read from the cluster and does not change at once.
catalogue.outcomeNotInstalled: Nothing to commit — <mono>{{app}}</mono> is not installed in this tenant.
catalogue.outcomeUninstalled: Uninstalling <mono>{{app}}</mono> was committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono> and takes effect on the next sync. This list is read from the cluster and does not change at once.
catalogue.outcomeUpdated: Moving <mono>{{app}}</mono> to this build was committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono> and arrives on the next sync. This list is read from the cluster and does not change at once.
catalogue.seeThemInTheApp: See them in the App Store
catalogue.storeOnly_one: {{count}} further entry is maintained or licensed and not listed here.
catalogue.storeOnly_other: {{count}} further entries are maintained or licensed and not listed here.
catalogue.theyAreTheStoreS: They are the App Store’s to present.
catalogue.thisCatalogueSourceCouldNot: This catalogue source could not be read. It is a web server outside the cluster; nothing here is broken.
catalogue.thisClusterNamesNoCatalogue: This cluster names no catalogue sources. They are declared on the Cluster claim, under
catalogue.uninstallConfirm: Uninstall {{app}} from {{tenant}}? The app is removed for everybody who uses it. Its data stays until it is purged.

clusterSettings.clusterSettingsAreUnavailableThis: Cluster settings are unavailable. This needs the cluster's audit relation, and the director has to be reachable from this console.
clusterSettings.committedAs: Committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. The cluster changes once Argo CD has synced it.
clusterSettings.lead: What <mono>{{cluster}}</mono> is configured with. Each change is a commit to the deployments repository with you as its author, which Argo CD then applies. Nothing here is written to the cluster directly.
clusterSettings.notSetNoDefault: not set — and the schema applies no default
clusterSettings.nothingToCommitTheCluster: Nothing to commit — the cluster already held those values.

credentials.anAdditiveAppCatalogueFor: An additive app catalogue for this tenant. Its apps appear alongside the cluster's; removing it removes those apps.
credentials.credentialsCannotBeReadRight: Credentials cannot be read right now.
credentials.name: Name
credentials.noCredentialsAreDeclaredFor: No credentials are declared for your scope.
credentials.noRepositoriesAreConfiguredFor: No repositories are configured for your scope.
credentials.unsatisfied_one: {{count}} required credential is not yet supplied.
credentials.unsatisfied_other: {{count}} required credentials are not yet supplied.
credentials.valuesAreWriteOnlyThis: Values are write-only. This shows whether a credential is present, who set it and when — never the value itself. A lost credential is rotated, not recovered.
credentials.whereYourAppsComeFrom: Where your apps come from. The cluster's own repositories are listed but not editable — your apps depend on them.

customizationDebt.aCheaperRungIsNow: A cheaper rung is now available
customizationDebt.lead: Every deviation from an app as shipped, tracked as a Customization record. Lower rungs (L0–L1) are routine; rungs L4 and above are carried deltas that must be reviewed, forwarded upstream, and eventually dropped. See the customization ladder.

integrations.activeIntegrationbindingsAreOperatorWire: Active IntegrationBindings are operator-wired. AppGrants are tenant-approved capability subsets synced to OpenFGA. Contract NetworkPolicies allow egress only for granted capabilities.
integrations.noAppgrantObjectsYetCreated: No AppGrant objects yet (created when consumer bindings exist).

models.addInstance: Add a model of this cluster
models.apiBase: Address (public https address, up to and including the version segment)
models.apiKeyProperty: Property that holds its token (follows from the name)
models.committedAs: Committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. The gateway restarts with these models once Argo CD has synced it; until then the list below is what git declares, not what the gateway runs.
models.credentialsUnreadable: Whether its token is supplied cannot be shown: the credentials list could not be read with your account.
models.enabledHint: Off, the gateway offers no model at all.
models.gatewayConsole: Serve the gateway's own console at a public address
models.gatewayConsoleWarning: Warning: this opens a public address, llm.<cluster domain>, for the gateway's own console and its whole API, behind the sign-in of the cluster's administrators. Switching it on or off is a commit and needs no run of the installer: the address and the network rule that lets it reach the gateway both follow that commit, each at the cluster's next synchronisation. For the moment between the two, the address may exist and answer nothing.
models.gpuAcceleration: This cluster has GPUs to serve models on
models.gpuAccelerationHint: The models of this cluster below are read only when this is on.
models.instancesHint: Models served from this cluster's own GPUs. The platform does not start the server behind such a model yet, so every one of them is listed by the gateway and flagged as not served until somebody runs it.
models.lead: The models the gateway of <mono>{{cluster}}</mono> offers. They come from the Cluster claim and from nowhere else: a model that is not on this screen is removed from the gateway, whoever added it and however. Each change is a commit to the deployments repository with you as its author.
models.newProviderHint: The cluster declares a credential for every provider committed here, with no further step. It appears on the Credentials screen once the cluster has applied the commit; until its token is supplied the provider's models are flagged below and answer an authentication error.
models.noCredentialNote: There is no credential {{credential}} that you can see. The cluster declares it once it has applied the claim that names this provider; if it stays missing, the cluster does not yet run a version that does. Until the token is supplied the model answers an authentication error.
models.nothingToCommit: Nothing to commit — the claim already declared these models.
models.offeredHint: As committed, under the names an app asks for. The status is worked out from the claim and the credentials list; the gateway itself is not asked, and nothing probes a model.
models.providersHint: OpenAI-compatible services the gateway calls, at public https addresses only. A model is offered as provider name/model name. No token is entered here, and a provider reads its own token only.
models.title: Models
models.tokenHint: The token is entered on the Credentials screen under <mono>{{credential}}</mono>, never here.
models.tokenMissingNote: The token has not been supplied under {{credential}}. The model is listed and answers an authentication error until it is.
models.tokenSuppliedNote: Not probed: a wrong token or an address that cannot be reached shows as a failing call.
models.unavailable: The models are unavailable. This needs the cluster's audit relation, and the director has to be reachable from this console.
models.wrongPropertyNote: The credential {{credential}} has no property {{property}}, so the gateway finds no token for this model.

notifications.couldNotLoad: The notifications could not be loaded: {{reason}}
notifications.groupsCouldNotLoad: The groups could not be loaded: {{reason}}
notifications.noNotificationsPublishedForThis: No notifications published for this tenant yet.
notifications.publishScopedBroadcastsToWorkspace: Publish scoped broadcasts to workspace members. Delivered to the shell notification inbox (v1 — no external email or chat consumers yet).
notifications.title: Title

platformSecurity.approveMacWaiversRequestedBy: Approve MAC waivers requested by catalogue ComponentProfiles. Workloads receive waiver pod labels only when both the profile declares a request and the cluster allows it.
platformSecurity.needCanAudit: The cluster’s bindings need can_audit, which is the security officer’s and the auditor’s. Nothing is wrong if you hold neither.
platformSecurity.noCatalogueProfilesCurrentlyRequest: No catalogue profiles currently request MAC waivers.
platformSecurity.readOnlyRolesAreGranted: Read-only. Roles are granted by putting somebody in a Keycloak group, and what each role carries is the authorization model’s to say, not this screen’s.
platformSecurity.unheldRoles_one: {{count}} role is held by nobody. For break-glass that is the intended state.
platformSecurity.unheldRoles_other: {{count}} roles are held by nobody. For break-glass that is the intended state.

resources.aWorkspaceRunsUnderA: A workspace runs under a ceiling — how much CPU, memory and storage its apps may claim between them. Changing plan commits the new ceiling to the deployments repository, the same path an app install takes, so what is running and what is recorded never disagree.
resources.ceilingDrifted: The ceiling in force is not the one {{plan}} describes. The cluster enforces what is there; what is billed is what is recorded. Re-applying a plan settles both.
resources.liveConsumption: Live consumption is {{source}}. Committed figures come from the quota the cluster enforces and are unaffected.
resources.noPlanIntervalsInThis: No plan intervals in this window.
resources.noResourcePlansAreDefined: No resource plans are defined on this cluster.
resources.noSamplesInThisWindow: No samples in this window. The platform records a workspace's ceiling and consumption on a timer, so history begins when sampling was switched on.
resources.nothingIsRecordedAboutThe: Nothing is recorded about the plan in force when this window opened, so the table below covers only the changes inside it.
resources.plansLeadAdmin: Changing a tenant's plan commits to the deployments repository and Argo CD applies it on the next sync.
resources.plansLeadTenant: Pick the plan this workspace should run on. A larger plan takes effect once the change syncs; a smaller one is refused while more than it allows is in use.
resources.theClusterOverviewCouldNot: The cluster overview could not be loaded.
resources.theResourcesApiCouldNot: The resources API could not be reached. Plans and usage are unavailable until it is.
resources.theUsageHistoryCouldNot: The usage history could not be loaded.
resources.thisWorkspaceRunsWithoutA: This workspace runs without a ceiling — its apps may claim whatever the cluster has.
resources.thisWorkspaceSCeilingWas: This workspace's ceiling was set by hand and matches no plan in the catalogue, so nothing prices it. Moving it onto a plan is what makes it invoiceable.
resources.whatThisWindowResolvesTo: What this window resolves to for invoicing: each stretch the workspace spent on one plan, and the SKU in effect over it.

securityPolicies.maxPasswordAgeInDays: Max password age in days (0 = off)
securityPolicies.passwordAlsoRequires: The realm also requires, and saving keeps:
securityPolicies.passwordNotReadable: You may not read this realm's password policy, so it is not shown and saving does not change it.
securityPolicies.passwordSetOnTheRealm: Set on the realm when you save, and in force at once.

tenants.committedAs: Committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. Provisioning follows once Argo CD has synced it.
tenants.couldNotCreate: The tenant could not be created.
tenants.couldNotRetire: The tenant could not be retired.
tenants.eachTenantIsAManifest: Each tenant is a manifest in the deployments repository. Bringing one on is a commit; the realm, the namespaces, the database and the desktop follow when Argo CD syncs it.
tenants.lowerCaseLettersDigitsAnd: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. This becomes the namespace, the realm, the database prefix and the hostname, so it cannot be changed later.
tenants.name: Name
tenants.tenantsAreUnavailableThisNeeds: Tenants are unavailable. This needs the cluster's audit relation, and the director has to be reachable from this console.
tenants.thisTenantCarriesTheRealm: This tenant carries the realm every administrator signs in against, so it cannot be retired here.
tenants.whatPeopleCallThisCustomer: What people call this customer. Can be changed at any time.
tenants.activateLead: The account has no password. Its holder sets one — and a second factor, unless switched off — through a single-use link.
tenants.recoveryEmailHint: Optional. The activation link, and later a password reset, go there. Without it the link is shown here, once.
tenants.requireMFA: The administrator must set up a second factor when activating
tenants.waitingForProvisioning: The tenant is being provisioned; the link is issued as soon as its account exists…
tenants.activationMailed: The activation link for {{user}} was sent to {{email}}.
tenants.activationLinkLead: Give this link to the administrator of {{user}}. It works once.
tenants.activationLinkHint: Valid until {{expires}}. It sets the password; nobody else ever knows it. It is not shown again — issue a new one if it is lost.
tenants.modeRetireBody: The tenant leaves the cluster: its desktop and apps stop and nobody can sign in to it. Its realm, databases and files are kept (its manifest's deletion policy, Retain unless someone changed it), so adding the tenant again brings it back.
tenants.modePurgeBody: The tenant leaves the cluster and its data goes with it: the realm and every account in it, its databases, files, mail and secrets. This cannot be undone. The tenant is listed as purging until the cluster has taken the deletion in.
tenants.purgingHint: Its data is set to be deleted; the tenant is removed as soon as the cluster has taken that in.
tenants.keepBundlesBody: The backup bucket and the bundles in it stay. For a tenant that was handed a copy and whose provider keeps one under contract; otherwise the backups go with everything else.
tenants.activationNotMailed: The realm cannot send mail yet (the SMTP relay is supplied in Credentials), so the link is shown here. {{email}} is kept as the recovery address.

requireAuth.howToConfigure: Set OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_CLIENT_ID on the web container, or AUTH_DISABLED=true for local dev. Behind the platform’s edge the platform sets AUTH_MODE=edge and none of these is needed.

members.title: Members
members.lead: Who is in this tenant, what they may open, and how they sign in.
members.cannotBeRead: Members cannot be read right now.
members.inviteLead: They get a link to set their password; nobody else ever knows it.
members.inviteEmailHint: Where the invitation and later password resets are sent.
members.requireTotpOnAccept: Require two-factor authentication when they accept
members.createdNotMailed: {{login}} was created, but the invitation did not go out. Send a password reset from their page.
members.totpConfigured: An authenticator app is set up.
members.totpPending: They must set up an authenticator app at their next sign-in.
members.resetSent: A password reset link was sent to {{email}}.
members.totpMailed: A link to set up two-factor authentication was sent to {{email}}.
members.removeLead: Their account is deleted and they can no longer sign in. This person has a mailbox on this cluster's mail server, and removing them does not decide what becomes of it. You do.
members.mailboxArchiveBody: The mail is kept. The mailbox is moved out of the mail server's live mailboxes: nobody receives mail or signs in at the address any more, and somebody who is given the same address later starts with an empty mailbox. The archived mailbox is part of the tenant's backups, is listed below under “Mailboxes of removed people”, and stays until an administrator deletes it there or the tenant is deleted.
members.mailboxDeleteBody: The mailbox and all the mail in it are destroyed. Deleting cannot be undone: only a backup taken before now still holds the mail.
members.mailboxDeleteConfirm: Delete the mailbox {{mailbox}} with all the mail in it? This cannot be undone.
members.removeChooseFirst: Choose first what becomes of the mailbox
members.removedMailboxesLead: What was decided about the mailbox of each person removed from this tenant, and what became of it. An archived mailbox is kept until it is deleted here or the tenant is deleted. Deleting it cannot be undone.
members.deleteArchivedConfirm: Delete the archived mailbox of {{address}} with all the mail in it? This cannot be undone.

groups.title: Groups
groups.lead: The groups members are put in: one per app, the tenant's roles, and any you make.
groups.cannotBeRead: Groups cannot be read right now.
groups.name: Name
groups.deleteConfirm: Delete the group {{name}}? Its members stay; only the group goes.

export.title: Export
export.lead: An export captures this workspace -- its apps' databases, files, volumes and its members -- into one encrypted bundle, staged in the cluster's own storage. Apps are paused one at a time while it runs.
export.opsTitle: Scheduled backups, kept off-site, restored in one click
export.opsLead: Export is yours whenever you want it. The Operations Console looks after it for you -- an Aluvian app, free for organisations under fifty users.
export.opsScheduled: Backups on a schedule, deduplicated, with retention you set
export.opsRemote: Copies at a destination of your own, immutable against ransomware
export.opsRecovery: Recovery and restore drills, one click each
export.opsInstalling: The Operations Console is being installed ({{phase}}).
export.opsInstall: Install 'operations-console' from the App Store to get them.

import.title: Import a tenant from a bundle
import.lead: The way back for an export, on this cluster or another: the tenant is declared from the bundle's own manifest, provisioned, and the data restored into it.
import.keyHint: The passphrase the export was taken with, or the age identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-…) that opens it. It is kept only as long as the restore runs.
import.name: Name
import.nameHint: Optional. The bundle names the tenant it came from; give another name to bring it up beside the original.
import.phase_declared: <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> is committed; the operator provisions it next.
import.passwordReset: Members have no credentials yet: send them a password reset, and activate the administrator from the list above.

licenceReport.title: Licence report
licenceReport.lead: What this cluster reports about what it runs. The report contains no names or addresses, only addresses of the cluster and its tenants and counts.
licenceReport.unavailable: The licence report is not available.
licenceReport.off: Licence reporting is turned off on this cluster. Nothing is sent, and the App Store is not offered.
licenceReport.noAttempt: No report has been due yet.
licenceReport.reasonSigningKeyAbsent: The cluster has no signing key for its reports, so nothing was sent.
licenceReport.reasonSigningKeyInvalid: The cluster's signing key for its reports cannot be used, so nothing was sent.
licenceReport.reasonInventoryUnavailable: The cluster could not work out what it runs, so nothing was sent.
licenceReport.reasonEndpointUnreachable: The address the report is sent to could not be reached. It is tried again.
licenceReport.reasonEndpointRefused: The receiving end refused the report. It is tried again.
licenceReport.sequence: Report number {{sequence}}, indented here for reading.
licenceReport.nothingSent: No report has been sent yet.

apps.title: Apps
apps.installNote: Apps are installed from the App Store, or with kubectl gentian apps install where no store is available. This page looks after the ones that are installed.
apps.declaredUnavailable: What git declares for this tenant could not be read, so the list below is only what the cluster reports.
apps.statesUnavailable: What the cluster has made of the apps could not be read, so the list below is only what git declares.
apps.none: No apps are installed in this tenant.
apps.notRolledOut: Declared, not on the cluster yet
apps.beingRemoved: No longer declared, still on the cluster
apps.declaredNo: Not declared: it has been uninstalled, and the cluster is still taking it down
apps.noComponent: The cluster reports no component for this app. It was committed and has not been rolled out yet, or the rollout has not started.
apps.everyoneIsOn: This app is for everyone: every member of this tenant has access by default, and people invited later get it pre-selected.
apps.everyoneIsOff: This app is not for everyone: access is given per person, below.
apps.everyoneOnConfirm: Make {{app}} for everyone in {{tenant}}? Every member gets access to it, and people invited later get it pre-selected.
apps.everyoneOffConfirm: Stop giving {{app}} to everyone in {{tenant}}? People who already have access keep it. People invited later no longer get it automatically.
apps.everyoneNotDeclared: Git does not declare this app, so there is nothing to switch.
apps.peopleLead: Whoever is in the app’s group <mono>{{group}}</mono> has access. Ticking a person gives it to them; unticking takes it away.
apps.noGroupYet: This app has no group yet. The cluster makes it when the app is ready; until then nobody can be given access.
apps.integrationsNone: This app consumes nothing from another app and offers nothing to one.
apps.privilegesLead: What this app asked of the platform beyond its default posture, and what was answered. Read-only: a request is not approved on this page.
apps.pendingUnknown: The cluster reports no component for this app, so what is waiting for approval is not known.
apps.approvedUnavailable: What has been approved could not be read.
apps.privilegesNone: Nothing is waiting for approval and nothing has been approved for this app.
apps.privilegeWaitingDetail: Nobody has approved this yet. The app waits until somebody does.
apps.privilegeDetailNotAvailable: What each request permits, and the app’s own reason for asking, are not available yet: only the name of the request is.
apps.uninstallLead: Removes the app and signs everyone out of it. Its files, database, object storage and stored credentials are kept, and people keep their access; a later install finds the data again. To destroy the data, purge it afterwards.
apps.uninstallConfirm: Uninstall {{app}} from {{tenant}}? This removes the app and signs everyone out of it. Its files, database, object storage and stored credentials are kept, and people keep their access. A later install finds the data again. To destroy the data, purge it afterwards.
apps.alreadyUninstalled: This app has been uninstalled; the cluster is still taking it down. Its data is kept. Once removal has finished, the app appears below under “Uninstalled apps with retained data”, where its data can be purged.
apps.outcomeEveryoneOn: Making <mono>{{app}}</mono> for everyone was committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. Every member gets access once the cluster has synced.
apps.outcomeEveryoneOff: <mono>{{app}}</mono> is no longer given to everyone: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. People who already have access keep it.
apps.outcomeAccessUnchanged: Nothing to commit — <mono>{{app}}</mono> already said so.
apps.outcomeUninstalled: Uninstalling <mono>{{app}}</mono> was committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono> and takes effect on the next sync. Its data is kept: once removal has finished, <mono>{{app}}</mono> appears below under “Uninstalled apps with retained data”.
apps.outcomeNotInstalled: Nothing to commit — <mono>{{app}}</mono> is not installed in this tenant.
apps.purgeNameInvalid: An app’s name is lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
apps.purgeStillInstalled: <mono>{{app}}</mono> is still installed. Only the data of an uninstalled app can be purged; uninstall it first.
apps.purgeDialogBody: Purging destroys what <mono>{{app}}</mono> holds in <mono>{{tenant}}</mono>: its files, its database, its object storage, its stored credentials, and its access group with every membership of it.
apps.retainedLead: Uninstalling an app keeps what it stored. These apps are no longer installed and still hold data; installing one again finds its data, and purging it destroys the data for good.
apps.retainedReading: Reading which uninstalled apps still hold data…
apps.retainedUnavailable: Which uninstalled apps still hold data could not be read.
apps.retainedNoneChecked: No uninstalled app with retained data was found among what could be checked.
apps.retainedIncomplete: The cluster could not check everything, so this list may be incomplete.
apps.kindExtensionCredentials: Stored credentials of the app’s extensions
apps.kindExtensionGroups: Access groups of the app’s extensions
apps.kindChartNamedFiles: Volumes that carry only the name of the app’s chart
apps.purgeNeedsProfile: Purge is refused until the app’s profile is available on this cluster again: without it, what the app owns cannot be determined.
apps.purgeDialogKept: Not destroyed: the entries the app wrote to the shared cache.
apps.purgeDialogFinal: This cannot be undone. It may take several minutes.
apps.purgeRunningBody: The data is being destroyed. This may take several minutes. Keep this page open; the result is shown here as soon as the cluster has answered.
apps.purgeComplete: The purge of <mono>{{app}}</mono> is complete: its data was destroyed.
apps.purgeIncomplete: INCOMPLETE: the purge of <mono>{{app}}</mono> did not cover everything the app may hold.
apps.purgeNotExamined: Not examined, and possibly still there:
apps.purgeFailed: The purge of <mono>{{app}}</mono> did not complete.
apps.purgeRetryHint: Retrying is safe: it continues with what is left.
apps.leftoversLead: Pieces that earlier builds of this app or of its active add-ons brought to the cluster and that the builds installed now no longer bring. Nothing removes them automatically: an older build that needed one would still find it.
apps.leftoversNotOnCluster: The cluster does not have this app installed in this tenant, so there is nothing it can report here.
apps.leftoversUnavailable: What updates left behind could not be read.
apps.leftoversIncomplete: The cluster could not check everything, so this report may be incomplete.
apps.leftoversShared: These pieces are shared by every tenant that uses this app. Ask the platform admin to remove them.
apps.leftoverDropped: The build installed now no longer brings it
apps.leftoverOrphaned: The app it belongs to is no longer on the cluster
apps.leftoverDeleting: The cluster accepted the deletion of <mono>{{name}}</mono> and still holds it. It is gone once the cluster has finished; until then it stays on this list.
apps.leftoverOtherAnswer: The cluster answered <mono>{{status}}</mono> for <mono>{{name}}</mono>. That is not an answer this page knows as a deletion; the list below shows what is on the cluster now.
apps.leftoverRefused: <mono>{{name}}</mono> was not deleted. The cluster refused, and gave this reason:
apps.leftoverForbidden: <mono>{{name}}</mono> was not deleted: you may not delete it.
apps.leftoverNotDone: <mono>{{name}}</mono> was not deleted. The answer was:
apps.leftoverUnknown: Whether <mono>{{name}}</mono> was deleted is not known: the request was not answered as expected. The list below was read again and shows what is on the cluster now.
apps.leftoverDialogBody: This deletes from the cluster: {{kind}} <mono>{{name}}</mono>. It is a piece an earlier build of <mono>{{app}}</mono> brought and the build installed now no longer brings.
apps.leftoverDialogDowngrade: If <mono>{{app}}</mono> is moved back to an older build that needed this piece, that build would no longer find it.
apps.leftoverDialogInEffect: This sign-in configuration is still in effect. Deleting it changes how the sign-in clients it configures are set up the next time they are configured.
apps.leftoverDialogFinal: This cannot be undone. Nothing puts the piece back except installing a build that brings it.
apps.publicLead: What this app asks to have on the internet, and whether that was approved. Installing the app publishes nothing. The same list shows a request that is not a public address: an entry behind sign-in that asks to keep the app's own Authorization header. The tenant's perimeter approver approves an entry here, or with the command <mono>kubectl gentian exposures approve</mono>.
apps.publicUnavailable: The public addresses and requests of this app could not be read.
apps.publicCredentialToApp: None at the platform's edge: the app checks the caller's credential
apps.publicRequestedDetailSignIn: Not approved. The header is removed, as on any entry behind sign-in.
apps.publicWithdrawConfirmSignIn: Withdraw {{name}} of tenant {{tenant}}? It is not a public address and nothing is taken down. Once the cluster has taken that in, the app's own Authorization header is removed again at {{address}}, and calls the app's pages make with it will be refused by the app. It can be approved again later.
apps.publicOutcomeApprovedSignIn: Approved <mono>{{name}}</mono>: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. Nothing is published. Once the cluster has taken that in, the app's own Authorization header is kept on that address behind sign-in.
apps.publicOutcomeWithdrawnSignIn: Withdrawn <mono>{{name}}</mono>: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. Once the cluster has taken that in, the app's own Authorization header is removed again.
apps.publicApproveIntroSignIn: Approving <mono>{{name}}</mono> for tenant <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> puts nothing on the internet. It changes this, behind sign-in:
apps.publicReviewIntroSignIn: <mono>{{name}}</mono> of tenant <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> is approved already; approving it again is a review. Nothing of it is on the internet. Behind sign-in, it has this:
apps.publicOnlyThese: Nothing else at this address is published.
apps.publicAnyone: Anyone on the internet, without sign-in
apps.publicCheckedByApp: Nobody signs in at the platform's edge. The app says it checks callers itself ({{mode}}); the platform does not check that.
apps.publicReviewDueDetail: Still published. Its review was due on {{review}}.
apps.publicExpiredDetail: Approved until {{until}}. Nothing is published any more.
apps.publicNoEnd: No end date: it stays until it is withdrawn.
apps.publicNotApprover: You are not a perimeter approver of this tenant, so approving and withdrawing are not offered to you here.
apps.publicNoApproveNowhere: Cannot be approved: it would be published nowhere.
apps.publicNoActionNotShown: Not reviewed or withdrawn here: the director cannot show what this entry publishes. Use <mono>kubectl gentian exposures</mono>.
apps.publicWithdrawConfirm: Withdraw {{name}} of tenant {{tenant}}? The platform takes it down, and {{address}} stops answering once the cluster has taken that in. It can be approved again later.
apps.publicWithdrawConfirmNoAddress: Withdraw {{name}} of tenant {{tenant}}? It has no address at the moment, so nothing is taken down; its approval is removed from the registry. It can be approved again later.
apps.publicWithdrawConfirmUnmatched: Withdraw {{name}} of tenant {{tenant}}? It matches nothing an installed app declares and nothing is published for it; this clears it from the registry.
apps.publicOutcomeApproved: Approved <mono>{{name}}</mono>: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. The platform publishes it once the cluster has taken that in.
apps.publicOutcomeReviewed: Reviewed <mono>{{name}}</mono>: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. Its review date, end date and reason are the new ones once the cluster has taken that in.
apps.publicOutcomeUnchanged: <mono>{{name}}</mono> is approved on these terms already; nothing was committed.
apps.publicOutcomeWithdrawn: Withdrawn <mono>{{name}}</mono>: committed as <mono>{{commit}}</mono>. The platform takes it down, and its address stops answering once the cluster has taken that in.
apps.publicOutcomeNotPublished: <mono>{{name}}</mono> was not published; nothing was committed.
apps.publicApproveIntro: Approving <mono>{{name}}</mono> for tenant <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> puts this on the internet:
apps.publicApproveIntroExpired: <mono>{{name}}</mono> of tenant <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> was approved until {{until}} and is not published any more. Approving it again puts this on the internet:
apps.publicReviewIntro: <mono>{{name}}</mono> of tenant <mono>{{tenant}}</mono> is approved already; approving it again is a review. It has this on the internet:
apps.publicRefusedDetail: Never published, also below a path above.
apps.publicSoFarReplaced: The end date and the reason below replace the ones it has.
apps.publicExpiresHint: Without a date it stays until it is withdrawn. With one the approval ends at the end of that day, UTC. It is reviewed a year from now at the latest, or at its end date if that is sooner.
apps.publicRecorded: Your name and the time are recorded with the entry.
apps.publicMainRuleTitle: This entry is for the cluster's main address. What the director says of a website there:
apps.publicMainRuleAcknowledge: I have read this rule and it is true of this site. My name and the time are recorded with the entry as the acknowledgement.
apps.publicMainRuleMissing: The director sent no rule for the main address, so there is nothing to acknowledge and this entry cannot be approved here.
